content.text: {"affected_statement":"L1.2","objection_correct":"yes","established_elsewhere":"yes","elsewhere_quote":"A positive integer is uniquely determined by its exponents $v_p(\\cdot)$, and only primes dividing some initial $a_i$ contribute; hence\n$$\\boxed{\\,M \\;=\\; \\prod_{p\\ \\mathrm{prime}} p^{\\,\\gcd\\big(v_p(a_1),\\, v_p(a_2),\\, \\dots,\\, v_p(a_N)\\big)}\\,}$$","status_as_written":"false_display","repair_distance":"sentence","explanation":"The objection is correct: if an absent prime q is allowed in d, then every positive v_q(d) divides the zero valuations, so arbitrary q-powers can be adjoined and no maximal d exists. The boxed valuation formula and its choice-independence are nevertheless proved correctly elsewhere. Restricting d to primes dividing at least one initial entry repairs the remark."}
